citation.snippet: grid_rows = sum(1 for ls in row_lanes.values() if len(ls) >= _MIN_LANES_PER_ROW)

citation_detail.actual_line: grid_rows = sum(1 for ls in row_lanes.values() if len(ls) >= _MIN_LANES_PER_ROW)

rows.rationale: has_numeric_columns clusters numeric-token x-positions into lanes and counts rows populating >= _MIN_LANES_PER_ROW lanes, with no lane-reuse requirement. A corrupt text layer (upside-down OCR) manufactures spurious numeric tokens scattered across ~30 nearly-unique lanes, which the gate reads as a row x column grid, so pure prose pages are classified as borderless tables. The issue's own direction (a lane-reuse ratio, tokens-per-occupied-lane) separates real tables from encoding noise without a magic threshold, but it explicitly 'wants measuring across the corpus before adoption' in both directions to avoid dropping real borderless tables — hence medium confidence.
